content.thinking:
I'm planning content for a July 18th post and need to find a fresh angle after twelve consecutive days of divergence pieces. I'm weighing a few options: comparing Nykaa against Honasa in the beauty space with an 11x valuation gap, or revisiting the DMart angle but from a different lens—patient retail versus quick commerce burn—though I used DMart in an April post so I need to be careful about repetition.

boAt versus global audio brands is interesting since boAt dominates India's audio market, but valuations are murky. Maruti versus Hyundai India could work now that Hyundai India went public in 2024, though the valuation gap isn't particularly surprising. The Bajaj versus Hero MotoCorp angle is compelling—Hero is the world's largest motorcycle maker by volume yet worth a third of Bajaj—but I just covered motorcycles with the Enfield/Harley post, so running another two-wheeler comparison back-to-back feels too thematically repetitive. I'll hold that one for later. Titan versus jewelry retailers feels weak, Asian Paints was already covered in June, and I'm still exploring whether a banking angle with HDFC Bank versus PSU banks has legs.

Actually, HDFC Bank versus SBI is a strong paradox: SBI has roughly 23 times more branches (22,740 versus 9,092) and significantly more deposits, yet HDFC Bank's market cap is double SBI's—around ₹15.2 lakh crore versus ₹7.3-8 lakh crore. The employee counts are surprisingly similar, so the real tension is branches and deposits versus valuation. That's a solid banger.

The takeaway is clean: "Efficiency beats empire" or "The market prices returns, not reach." Banking is a fascinating sector where India's biggest household names reveal how the market values operational efficiency over physical footprint. I should verify these numbers—HDFC Bank and SBI market caps, branch counts, and deposit figures—to make sure the comparison holds up.

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ tweet-card.py — render a tweet-style image card (Aviral Bhatnagar format). A clean square white card: avatar + name + verified badge + @handle, then big text. Matches how Aviral repurposes his tweets as LinkedIn image posts. Deterministic (HTML -> Chrome headless via html-to-png.py). No AI image gen. Usage: python3 tools/tweet-card.py --text "line1\\n\\nline2\\n\\nVerdict" --out card.png (defaults: Aditya Arora / @thefaadguy / drafts/images/_logos/aditya-avatar.jpg) Inline emphasis markup in --text: ~text~ -> yellow marker HIGHLIGHT __text__ -> thick UNDERLINE """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse, html, re, subprocess, tempfile, os from pathlib import Path REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent FONT_STACK = "'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" TEMPLATE = """
{name}
{handle}
{body}
""" def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--text", required=True, help="post text; use \\n for newlines") ap.add_argument("--out", required=True) ap.add_argument("--name", default="Aditya Arora") ap.add_argument("--handle", default="@thefaadguy") ap.add_argument("--avatar", default=str(REPO / "clients/aditya-arora/drafts/images/_logos/aditya-avatar.jpg")) args = ap.parse_args() body = html.escape(args.text.replace("\\n", "\n")) # emphasis markup (applied after escaping, so spans are safe to inject) body = re.sub(r"__([^_]+)__", r'\1', body) body = re.sub(r"~([^~]+)~", r'\1', body) doc = TEMPLATE.format(font=FONT_STACK, avatar=args.avatar, name=html.escape(args.name), handle=html.escape(args.handle), body=body) tmp = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "tweetcard.html" tmp.write_text(doc, encoding="utf-8") subprocess.run(["python3", str(REPO / "tools/html-to-png.py"), "--html", str(tmp), "--out", args.out, "--width", "1080", "--height", "1080"], check=True) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
founder-story-card.py — build a "founder story" infographic card.

Matches Aditya's highest-ER infographic format (1.1-1.5% ER, 150K-400K imp):
a REAL founder photo (4:5) with a bold bottom text-overlay hook, key phrases
in red. Deterministic (full pixel control) — no AI image gen, no drift.

Hook markup: lines separated by "||", red phrases wrapped in *asterisks*.
  "Born to a landless farmer.||His first salary was *Rs 150* a month.||He sold his company for *4,500 CR*."

Usage:
  python3 tools/founder-story-card.py --photo /tmp/vel.png \
      --lines "Born to a landless farmer.||His first salary was *Rs 150* a month.||He sold his company for *4,500 CR*." \
      --out clients/aditya-arora/drafts/images/2026-06-27-velumani.png
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
FONT = REPO / "tools/fonts/Montserrat-ExtraBold.ttf"
W, H = 1080, 1350           # 4:5
RED = (228, 30, 45)
BLACK = (20, 20, 20)
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
SIDE_PAD = 46               # text inset inside the white box
V_PAD = 48                  # vertical padding inside the box
LINE_GAP = 1.18             # line height multiplier


def crop_4x5(im: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
    im = im.convert("RGB")
    tw, th = W, H
    sr, tr = im.width / im.height, tw / th
    if sr > tr:                      # too wide -> crop sides
        nw = int(im.height * tr)
        im = im.crop(((im.width - nw) // 2, 0, (im.width - nw) // 2 + nw, im.height))
    else:                            # too tall -> crop top/bottom (bias up to keep face)
        nh = int(im.width / tr)
        top = int((im.height - nh) * 0.30)
        im = im.crop((0, top, im.width, top + nh))
    return im.resize((tw, th), Image.LANCZOS)


def parse_line(s: str):
    """'His first salary was *Rs 150* a month.' -> [(text,color),...]"""
    segs, red = [], False
    for part in s.split("*"):
        if part:
            segs.append((part, RED if red else BLACK))
        red = not red
    return segs


def line_width(segs, font):
    return sum(font.getbbox(t)[2] - font.getbbox(t)[0] for t, _ in segs)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--photo", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--lines", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--align", default="left", choices=["left", "center"])
    args = ap.parse_args()

    img = crop_4x5(Image.open(args.photo))
    lines = [parse_line(l) for l in args.lines.split("||")]

    # auto-fit font so the widest line fits W - 2*SIDE_PAD
    size = 92
    while size > 30:
        font = ImageFont.truetype(str(FONT), size)
        if max(line_width(l, font) for l in lines) <= W - 2 * SIDE_PAD:
            break
        size -= 2
    asc, desc = font.getmetrics()
    lh = int((asc + desc) * LINE_GAP)
    box_h = lh * len(lines) + 2 * V_PAD

    # composite a soft drop-shadow + white box so the card lifts off ANY background
    img = img.convert("RGBA")
    overlay = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    od = ImageDraw.Draw(overlay)
    box_top = H - box_h
    SHADOW = 22
    for k in range(SHADOW):
        a = int(85 * (k / SHADOW))            # 0 -> 85 alpha, darkest at the box edge
        od.line([(0, box_top - SHADOW + k), (W, box_top - SHADOW + k)], fill=(0, 0, 0, a))
    od.rectangle([0, box_top, W, H], fill=WHITE + (255,))
    img = Image.alpha_composite(img, overlay).convert("RGB")

    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    y = H - box_h + V_PAD
    for segs in lines:
        x = SIDE_PAD if args.align == "left" else (W - line_width(segs, font)) // 2
        for text, color in segs:
            draw.text((x, y), text, font=font, fill=color)
            x += font.getbbox(text)[2] - font.getbbox(text)[0]
        y += lh

    out = Path(args.out)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    img.save(out, "PNG")
    print(f"wrote {out} ({out.stat().st_size:,} bytes) | font {size}px | box {box_h}px | {len(lines)} lines")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""

Turns each approved reply in replies-batch.json into an `http.request` job on the
Snowball EC2 server, staggered 5-10 min apart so they trickle out like a human
working through their comments. Each job POSTs to Unipile's create-comment
endpoint with a comment_id (threaded reply).

SAFETY: defaults to --dry-run. Nothing is created until you pass --commit.

Usage:
  python3 schedule_replies.py --dry-run            # preview the schedule
  python3 schedule_replies.py --commit             # actually create the jobs
  python3 schedule_replies.py --commit --start "2026-06-23T16:30:00+05:30"
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, json, ssl, urllib.request, urllib.error
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

# deterministic-ish jitter without Math.random dependency; varies per index
GAPS_MIN = [7, 6, 9, 5, 8, 10, 6, 7, 9, 5, 8, 6, 10, 7, 5, 9, 6, 8, 7, 10, 5, 9, 6, 8, 7, 5, 10, 6, 9]

import os
REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
ENV = os.path.join(REPO, ".env")
BATCH = os.path.join(REPO, "clients/aditya-arora/reply-engine/replies-batch.json")

try:
    import certifi
    CTX = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
except Exception:
    CTX = ssl.create_default_context()


def read_env():
    env = {}
    for line in open(ENV):
        line = line.strip()
        if "=" in line and not line.startswith("#"):
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            env[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return env


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--commit", action="store_true", help="actually create jobs (default is dry-run)")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--start", default=None, help="ISO start time for first reply; default now+5min")
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="aditya-reply-engine")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    commit = args.commit and not args.dry_run

    env = read_env()
    api = env["SNOWBALL_API_BASE"].rstrip("/")
    api = api if api.endswith("/api") else api + "/api"
    token = env["SNOWBALL_API_TOKEN"]
    uni_base = env["UNIPILE_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/api/v1"
    uni_key = env["UNIPILE_API_KEY"]

    batch = json.loads(open(BATCH, encoding="utf-8").read())
    account = env[batch["account_env"]]
    replies = batch["replies"]

    if args.start:
        t = datetime.fromisoformat(args.start)
    else:
        t = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(minutes=5)
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)

    from urllib.parse import quote
    print(f"{'COMMIT' if commit else 'DRY-RUN'} | {len(replies)} replies | EC2 {api} | start {t.isoformat()}")
    print(f"window: ~{sum(GAPS_MIN[:len(replies)-1])} min (~{round(sum(GAPS_MIN[:len(replies)-1])/60,1)} h)\n")

    created = []
    for i, r in enumerate(replies):
        run_at = t.isoformat()
        url = f"{uni_base}/posts/{quote(r['social_id'], safe='')}/comments"
        payload = {
            "url": url,
            "method": "POST",
            "headers": {"X-API-KEY": uni_key, "Content-Type": "application/json", "accept": "application/json"},
            "body": {"account_id": account, "text": r["reply_text"], "comment_id": r["comment_id"]},
        }
        job = {"action": "http.request", "run_at": run_at, "tag": args.tag, "max_attempts": 2, "payload": payload}

        local = t.astimezone(timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))).strftime("%H:%M IST")
        print(f"[{i+1:2}] {local}  P{r['post_index']} -> {r['author'][:22]:22} | {r['reply_text'][:48]}...")

        if commit:
            data = json.dumps(job).encode()
            req = urllib.request.Request(api + "/jobs", data=data, method="POST",
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30, context=CTX) as resp:
                    res = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
                    r["job_id"] = res.get("id")
                    r["scheduled_fire"] = res.get("next_fire_at")
                    created.append(res.get("id"))
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                print("    ERROR:", e.code, e.read().decode()[:200])

        if i < len(replies) - 1:
            t = t + timedelta(minutes=GAPS_MIN[i % len(GAPS_MIN)])

    if commit:
        batch["scheduled_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        batch["job_ids"] = created
        open(BATCH, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(batch, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        print(f"\nCreated {len(created)} jobs on EC2. job_ids saved to batch file.")
        print(f"Cancel any time: DELETE {api}/jobs/<id>  (or by tag '{args.tag}')")
    else:
        print("\nDRY-RUN only. Re-run with --commit to create these jobs.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
fetch_comments.py — Reply Engine, step 1 (READ-ONLY).

Pulls a client's last N posts and every comment on them via Unipile, so we can
draft replies. No writes, no LinkedIn actions — just GETs on our own content.
Reusable across clients: pass the client slug + the .env account-id var name.

Usage:
  python3 fetch_comments.py \
      --slug thefaadguy \
      --account-env UNIPILE_ACCOUNT_ID_ADITYA \
      --posts 10 \
      --out clients/aditya-arora/reply-engine/comments-raw.json
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, json, ssl
from pathlib import Path
from urllib import error, parse, request

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ENV = REPO / ".env"

# Aditya's Unipile pod presents a cert the default store dislikes; the existing
# engagement engine disables verification for the Unipile host. Match that.
ssl._create_default_https_context = ssl._create_unverified_context


def read_env() -> dict:
    env = {}
    for line in ENV.read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if "=" in line and not line.startswith("#"):
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            env[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return env


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--slug", required=True, help="public_identifier, e.g. thefaadguy")
    ap.add_argument("--account-env", required=True, help=".env var holding this client's account_id")
    ap.add_argument("--posts", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    env = read_env()
    base = env["UNIPILE_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/api/v1"
    key = env["UNIPILE_API_KEY"]
    account = env[args.account_env]
    GH = {"X-API-KEY": key, "accept": "application/json"}

    def get(path, params):
        url = f"{base}{path}?{parse.urlencode(params)}"
        req = request.Request(url, headers=GH)
        try:
            with request.urlopen(req, timeout=40) as r:
                return json.loads(r.read().decode() or "{}")
        except error.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.read().decode()[:300]
            raise SystemExit(f"Unipile {e.code} on {path}: {body}")

    # 1) resolve provider_id + sanity
    prof = get(f"/users/{parse.quote(args.slug, safe='')}", {"account_id": account})
    provider_id = prof.get("provider_id")
    name = f"{prof.get('first_name','')} {prof.get('last_name','')}".strip()
    print(f"Account OK: {name} ({args.slug}) provider_id={provider_id} followers={prof.get('follower_count')}")

    # 2) posts (over-fetch, sort desc, take N)
    pdata = get(f"/users/{provider_id}/posts", {"account_id": account, "limit": max(args.posts * 3, 25)})
    posts = pdata.get("items", [])
    posts.sort(key=lambda p: p.get("parsed_datetime") or p.get("date") or "", reverse=True)
    posts = posts[: args.posts]
    print(f"Fetched {len(posts)} most-recent posts")

    # 3) comments per post
    out_posts = []
    total_comments = 0
    for i, p in enumerate(posts, 1):
        social_id = p.get("social_id")
        cdata = get(f"/posts/{parse.quote(social_id, safe='')}/comments", {"account_id": account})
        comments = cdata.get("items", [])
        total_comments += len(comments)
        snippet = (p.get("text") or "").replace("\n", " ")[:70]
        print(f"  [{i:2}] {p.get('comment_counter','?'):>3} comments | {snippet}")
        out_posts.append({
            "post_index": i,
            "social_id": social_id,
            "post_id": p.get("id"),
            "share_url": p.get("share_url"),
            "posted_at": p.get("parsed_datetime") or p.get("date"),
            "text": p.get("text"),
            "reaction_counter": p.get("reaction_counter"),
            "comment_counter": p.get("comment_counter"),
            "impressions_counter": p.get("impressions_counter"),
            "comments": comments,
        })

    out = {
        "client_slug": args.slug,
        "account_env": args.account_env,
        "provider_id": provider_id,
        "name": name,
        "posts": out_posts,
        "totals": {"posts": len(out_posts), "comments": total_comments},
    }
    outp = (REPO / args.out)
    outp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    outp.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    print(f"\nWrote {outp.relative_to(REPO)}  ({total_comments} comments across {len(out_posts)} posts)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
build_batch.py — Reply Engine, step 2 (DRAFT, no network).

Maps hand-written replies to specific fetched comments and emits a batch file
the scheduler consumes. Pure local: reads comments-raw.json, writes replies-batch.json.
Validates each target comment exists and is not the client's own comment.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import json
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
RAW = REPO / "clients/aditya-arora/reply-engine/comments-raw.json"
OUT = REPO / "clients/aditya-arora/reply-engine/replies-batch.json"

# (post_index 1-based, comment_index 0-based, reply_text)
REPLIES = [
    # ---- POST 1: Asian Paints (data/distribution moat) ----
    (1, 3, "Availability is exactly it, Bhavpreet. A product the customer can always find beats a better product they have to hunt for. Asian Paints understood that fifty years before it became a buzzword."),
    (1, 2, "Glad it landed, Sachin. The boring part stays a moat precisely because most people refuse to do it for ten years straight. That refusal is the advantage."),

    # ---- POST 2: Thums Up (customer-love moat) ----
    (2, 0, "Becoming the category itself is the real dream. When people ask for the brand instead of the product, both price and competition stop mattering as much."),
    (2, 8, "What hits the tongue, well put Ravit. Coca-Cola owned everything on paper and still could not move the one thing that mattered, the taste people had already chosen."),
    (2, 19, "Most people don't know it, Raghab. That is what makes it one of my favourite business stories. The brand they tried to bury outlived the plan to bury it."),

    # ---- POST 3: Flipkart Mafia ----
    (3, 11, "That is the real compounding, Sohail. One company that teaches people to build at scale ends up seeding the next twenty. The cap table exits, the operators stay."),
    (3, 9, "Flipsters is honestly better, Dnyanesh. Mafia sounds dramatic, but what they actually share is a playbook, not a payroll."),
    (3, 3, "Fair point, Mrityunjay. Mafia is just shorthand. The real story is that Flipkart handed them ownership and hard problems early, and that is what turned them into builders."),

    # ---- POST 4: $40B raised, where did it go ----
    (4, 13, "Money raised is not money made, that is the whole post in one line, Ansshav. Funding buys time and attention. What you do with that time is the actual business."),
    (4, 10, "The 100 for 70 trick built a lot of GMV in this country. It looks like demand right up until the discount stops, and then you find out if anyone actually wanted the product."),

    # ---- POST 5: D2C past Rs 1,000 Cr ----
    (5, 9, "You spotted the real lesson, Anish. Pure online has a ceiling in India. Crossing 1,000 crore almost always means becoming the offline retailer you set out to disrupt."),
    (5, 12, "Retention is the unglamorous half nobody posts about, Mukesh. Acquisition gets you the first sale. Repeat purchase is what actually builds a 1,000 crore brand."),
    (5, 19, "Good question, Vivek. The short version is they stopped treating supply chain as a back office. Inventory, warehousing and margins became founder-level decisions, not something delegated away."),

    # ---- POST 6: $20B in exits ----
    (6, 13, "Appreciate the detail, Nirmal. You are right that a big chunk of that was stock, not cash, and the Byju's fall hit it hard. The cash versus paper split is exactly the nuance these headline numbers hide."),
    (6, 6, "Buying speed is the honest reason behind most acquisitions, Mukul. It is cheaper to buy a working distribution engine than to spend three years building one and still arrive late."),
    (6, 4, "That is a mature way to read it, Afzal. The highest bid and the right home for a company are not always the same thing, and good founders think hard about who inherits what they built."),

    # ---- POST 7: Rs 12,500 Cr combined profit ----
    (7, 10, "Zerodha and Zoho are the proof, Viswaraj. No VC, no noise, just years of execution and customer money. Quiet compounding beats loud fundraising more often than the timeline suggests."),
    (7, 12, "Fair critique, Sathish. India is still better at building marketplaces than products. That gap is exactly where the next decade of opportunity sits for founders willing to go deep."),
    (7, 13, "Not a coincidence, Abhishek. When you are not optimising for the next round, you get to optimise for profit instead. The incentive shapes the outcome."),

    # ---- POST 8: Rs 100 Cr that wasn't (GMV) ----
    (8, 0, "The slice you control, exactly, Madhav. GMV is just traffic passing through your pipe. Take rate is what you actually keep, and that is the only number that pays salaries."),
    (8, 7, "The agent versus principal distinction is the whole game, Akshat. Booking gross when you only earn a commission is how a 100 crore company turns out to be a 6 crore one."),
    (8, 11, "This is the part most people miss, Deepak. Whatever number you celebrate internally is the number your team optimises for. Reward GMV and you will quietly buy revenue you cannot keep."),
    (8, 13, "Ha, fair, Vikrant. Though SpaceX has hard contracts and real margins sitting behind the vision. Burning money with a moat is very different from burning it to inflate a number."),

    # ---- POST 9: UPI ----
    (9, 3, "Genuine question deserves a real answer, Maahesh. UPI was never meant to earn on the transaction. It is public rail. The money sits on the layer above it, lending, commerce, data, and that layer is very much monetisable. Free at the base is what made the volume possible."),
    (9, 13, "You are right to flag that, Jim. The zero-MDR rule holds for bank account UPI. Rupay credit on UPI above 2,000 does carry a charge now. The free part is the rails, not every product riding on them."),
    (9, 9, "That is the real challenge, Ayushmaan. Abroad the model is government to government, not app to consumer. India exports the rails and the local regulator adopts them, which sidesteps a lot of the competition fight you are describing."),
    (9, 0, "I hear the same, Akhil. What fascinates them most is that it was built as open infrastructure, not a private wallet. That one design choice is the part the rest of the world is still studying."),

    # ---- POST 10: angel over-dilution ----
    (10, 13, "Could not agree more, Sramana. Premature dilution and dumb money compound in ways a first-time founder simply cannot see in month one. By the time the cost shows up, it is already locked in."),
    (10, 9, "Sharp pushback, Saurabh. You are right that when a company is dying, survival beats cap-table purity. My point is narrower. Plenty of founders give away 25% out of fear when a cleaner 12 to 15% was actually on the table. Desperation and a bad deal are not always the same thing."),
    (10, 6, "Ha, I walked into that one, Pranshu. Fair, 10% at 25 lakh is the clean ideal, not the daily reality. The honest range is closer to 12 to 18. The point stands though, 25% for a first cheque is the expensive end no matter how you cut it."),
]


def main() -> int:
    raw = json.loads(RAW.read_text())
    me = raw["provider_id"]
    by_idx = {p["post_index"]: p for p in raw["posts"]}

    items = []
    errors = []
    seen = set()
    for pi, ci, text in REPLIES:
        post = by_idx.get(pi)
        if not post:
            errors.append(f"P{pi}: no such post"); continue
        comments = post["comments"]
        if ci >= len(comments):
            errors.append(f"P{pi}C{ci}: index out of range ({len(comments)} comments)"); continue
        c = comments[ci]
        a = c.get("author_details") or {}
        if a.get("id") == me:
            errors.append(f"P{pi}C{ci}: targets client's OWN comment"); continue
        key = c["id"]
        if key in seen:
            errors.append(f"P{pi}C{ci}: duplicate comment_id"); continue
        seen.add(key)
        items.append({
            "post_index": pi,
            "social_id": post["social_id"],
            "post_id": post["post_id"],
            "comment_id": c["id"],
            "author": c.get("author"),
            "author_headline": a.get("headline"),
            "network_distance": (a.get("network_distance") or "").replace("DISTANCE_", "D"),
            "comment_text": c.get("text"),
            "reply_text": text,
        })

    if errors:
        print("VALIDATION ERRORS:")
        for e in errors:
            print("  -", e)

    OUT.write_text(json.dumps({
        "client_slug": raw["client_slug"],
        "account_env": raw["account_env"],
        "count": len(items),
        "replies": items,
    }, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    print(f"\nWrote {OUT.relative_to(REPO)} with {len(items)} replies "
          f"({len(REPLIES)} drafted, {len(errors)} errors).")
    return 1 if errors else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for reading and writing to .pen files and gives you tools to be an expert design generator and validator specifically for web and mobile applications and websites.

- IMPORTANT: The contents of the .pen files are encrypted and can be only access via the "pencil" MCP tools. DO NOT use "Read" or "Grep" tools to read contents of .pen files.
- IMPORTANT: Make sure to ONLY use the "pencil" MCP tools when reading or searching contents of .pen files (batch_get) and making changes inside .pen files (batch_design).
- IMPORTANT: Always follow the tool definitions and formats for the "pencil" MCP tools.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Asian Paints' founding:

## Founding in 1942

Asian Paints was founded by four friends - Champaklal Choksi, Chimanlal Choksi, Suryakant Dani, and Arvind Vakil in 1942, during a time when India was still under British colonial rule.

## Garage in Bombay

Champaklal and others initially functioned out of a garage in Bombay that was rented at INR 75 per month. More specifically, the business was founded in a garage in Gaiwadi, Girgaon, Mumbai.

## Connection to Quit India Movement and Paint Import Ban

In February 1942, while Mahatma Gandhi was preparing for the Quit India Movement, the British had imposed a temporary ban on paint imports due to World War II, leaving India with only Shalimar Paints and expensive foreign brands. This timing and situation created the opportunity for the four friends to establish Asian Paints to meet local demand.

## Early Growth

In 1945, the partnership firm turned itself into a private limited company following a turnover of INR 0.35 million that year. The company has been the market leader in paints since 1967.

Done, sir. Answering your first question: **you had exactly 1 post left** — Marico, firing today at 10:00 AM. The queue now runs **11 deep, unbroken through 16 August**.

## What the data said

I pulled all 21 posts from the last three weeks. The top 5 (Titan/Wipro 269K · HDFC/SBI 258K · Bajaj Finance/Kotak 257K · Bajaj Auto/Hero 233K · Info Edge 224K) share one exact skeleton:

**Hook** states the valuation gap first — `[A] is worth around ₹X lakh Cr while [B] is worth about ₹Y lakh Cr` — with two household names, **both alive and strong**. **Block 2** gives the *physical* scale of the one worth less (branches, employees, units). **Block 3** delivers the market's verdict. **Block 4** is a 2–5 word aphorism. 320–385 chars, always.

The flops break it in four identifiable ways: an abstract institution with no rival (NSE, 16K), a repeated pairing (Eternal/Wipro, 16K — seven days after Titan/Wipro), a rival everyone knows is dying (SpiceJet 30K, Vodafone Idea 69K), or a single company with no valuation opponent (Zerodha 31K, MRF 26K). Profit milestones don't work; *valuation paradoxes* do.

## The 10 new posts — 7–16 August, 10:00 AM IST daily

| Date | Story | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Fri 7 | Nestlé India ₹2.93L Cr > Tata Steel ₹2.38L Cr | Snacks outvalue steel |
| Sat 8 | BEL ₹2.86L Cr > Wipro ₹1.84L Cr — on 8,844 vs 2,30,864 employees | Fewer hands, higher value |
| Sun 9 | Maruti ₹4.48L vs Mahindra ₹4.24L — 24 lakh vehicles vs 6.6 lakh SUVs | The SUV won the decade |
| Mon 10 | Trent ₹1.66L > Tata Consumer ₹1.08L — Zudio beats Tata Tea and Salt | The new Tata sells t-shirts |
| Tue 11 | HAL ₹3.10L > IndiGo ₹2.09L — 440 aircraft, 12.3 crore passengers | The jets beat the seats |
| Wed 12 | Varun Beverages ₹1.50L > Indian Hotels ₹1.05L — the Pepsi bottler beats the Taj | Distribution is the business |
| Thu 13 | HUL ₹5L > ITC ₹3.55L | Focus beats diversification |
| Fri 14 | Britannia ₹1.32L > Apollo Hospitals ₹1.27L | Biscuits compound quietly |
| **Sat 15** | **Asian Paints: 4 friends, a ₹75/month Bombay garage, 1942, imports banned, Quit India → ₹2.66L Cr** | Made in India, 1942 |
| Sun 16 | NTPC ₹3.36L > Coal India ₹2.58L — 768 million tonnes dug | Value moves downstream |

Previews follow the usual pattern, e.g. [Nestlé/Tata Steel](https://app.thesnowball.agency/preview-linkedin/2026-08-07-aditya-avtext-nestle-tatasteel), [HAL/IndiGo](https://app.thesnowball.agency/preview-linkedin/2026-08-11-aditya-avtext-hal-indigo), [Asian Paints](https://app.thesnowball.agency/preview-linkedin/2026-08-15-aditya-avtext-asianpaints-1942).

Three deliberate calls worth knowing about. **Aug 15 is Independence Day**, so I broke format once for the Asian Paints swadeshi origin story — it's the one day the emotional beat outperforms a valuation table. **Grok killed three candidates** I liked (Tata Consumer/Tata Steel, Varun/Nestlé, ITC/HUL overtake — all false), and it also asserted Haldiram's-beats-Nykaa-style claims I had to correct against its own numbers. And I **killed the Trent vs Tata Motors post**: that ticker is now the post-demerger commercial-vehicles entity only, so the market cap is ambiguous and the comments would have eaten it. Trent got paired with Tata Consumer instead.

Nine of ten are pure valuation paradoxes in the winning shape; every company is new to the series; every number is Grok-verified with a WebSearch cross-check and logged in the ledger. The formula is now written to memory so the next batch starts from it.

content.text:
Scheduled for today, 17 August, 10:00 AM IST — job 982, draft 117, sole item in the queue.

**Preview:** https://app.thesnowball.agency/preview-linkedin/2026-08-17-aditya-avtext-eternal-indianoil

**The post:** Eternal (Zomato + Blinkit) is worth ~₹3 lakh Cr; Indian Oil ~₹1.9 lakh Cr. Indian Oil earned **₹8.86 lakh Cr in revenue — over 16x Eternal's ₹54,364 Cr** — plus a record ₹36,802 Cr profit, from 40,000+ petrol pumps. The market still pays more for the app on your phone. Verdict: **"Growth is the only currency."**

Straight answer on the 300K target: I can't guarantee it — our ceiling so far is 269K, and reach is set by LinkedIn's algorithm, not by us. What I can do is stack every variable the data says matters, and this post does that better than anything we've run.

Here's what the six weeks actually taught me, and it corrected two of my own earlier assumptions:

| Tier | Posts | Shared trait |
|---|---|---|
| 248–269K | Titan/Wipro, HDFC/SBI, Bajaj Finance, **Varun/Taj** | Prestige inversion — the "obviously superior" side loses |
| 198–234K | Bajaj Auto/Hero, Maruti/Mahindra, Nestlé/Tata Steel, Info Edge | Big surprise, weaker status stake |
| 19–76K | BEL/Wipro, HAL/IndiGo, NTPC/Coal India, HUL/ITC, Britannia/Apollo | B2B/PSU subjects, or a gap too small to shock |

I was wrong about defence being hot — BEL did 49K and HAL 76K despite perfect execution. And I was wrong that "giant beats all challengers combined" travels; HUL/ITC did 24K because nobody is surprised HUL is big. **The engine is the size of the surprise plus whether the reader personally touches both brands.** Varun/Taj proved it at 248K: a Pepsi bottler beating the Taj.

This post takes the exact DNA of the 258K HDFC/SBI post ("size is not value") and pushes it to 16x extremity, with two things every Indian touches daily — a food-delivery app and a petrol pump. The verdict is deliberately arguable so the profit-vs-growth fight happens in the comments; comment volume is what carried the Tesla post to 194K with 137 comments.

One trap avoided: the widely-cited USD figures still show Tata Steel ahead of "Zomato," because that ticker died at the rename in May 2025. I used live ETERNAL data only. IOC is also framed at full strength — record profit, 40,000 pumps — so this reads as market psychology, not a dunk on a PSU, and it stays clear of the dying-rival pattern that sank the Vodafone Idea post.

Done, sir. The card now runs real brand logos inline where the names were.

**Preview:** https://app.thesnowball.agency/preview-linkedin/2026-08-17-aditya-avtext-eternal-indianoil

Live as **draft 119 / job 984**, still firing today at 10:00 AM IST. Queue verified at exactly one pending job.

Three things worth flagging from the build:

**The logos are the real ones**, pulled from Wikimedia's official brand files via the Wikipedia API — Indian Oil, Blinkit, and Zomato. Simple-icons only had Zomato (and only in monochrome), so that path wouldn't have worked.

**Indian Oil needed a crop.** Its official logo stacks the circular emblem above an "IndianOil" wordmark, and at inline size the wordmark turned to mush. I cropped the SVG viewBox to the emblem alone — the orange-and-navy roundel every Indian sees at a petrol pump — which is both more recognizable and legible at text size. I tested three treatments (small inline, large inline with the crop, and logo+name chips) before picking this one; the chips version was redundant since the logo already says the name.

**One trap caught:** the folder already had an old wide Zomato *wordmark* SVG from earlier infographics, and the resolver grabbed it first — it rendered as a giant red banner that swamped the layout. Swapped to the square app icon so all three marks sit in the same visual family.

I also built this into `tools/tweet-card.py` properly rather than one-off: any card can now write `{{slug}}` to drop in a logo, with the leading auto-opening when logos are present so the lines don't crowd. So every future client post can use this same treatment.

The caption is unchanged — LinkedIn body text can't carry images, so it still names all three companies in words, which is right since the caption is what gets read in the feed preview.

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ tweet-card.py — render a tweet-style image card (Aviral Bhatnagar format). A clean square white card: avatar + name + verified badge + @handle, then big text. Matches how Aviral repurposes his tweets as LinkedIn image posts. Deterministic (HTML -> Chrome headless via html-to-png.py). No AI image gen. Usage: python3 tools/tweet-card.py --text "line1\\n\\nline2\\n\\nVerdict" --out card.png (defaults: Aditya Arora / @thefaadguy / drafts/images/_logos/aditya-avatar.jpg) Inline emphasis markup in --text: ~text~ -> yellow marker HIGHLIGHT __text__ -> thick UNDERLINE {{slug}} -> inline brand LOGO, sized to sit in the line of text. Resolves /.{svg,png,jpg,webp}. Source real logos via tools/fetch-brand-logo.py (simple-icons) or the Wikipedia pageimages API for brands simple-icons lacks. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse, html, re, subprocess, tempfile, os import pathlib from pathlib import Path REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent FONT_STACK = "'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" TEMPLATE = """
{name}
{handle}
{body}
""" def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--text", required=True, help="post text; use \\n for newlines") ap.add_argument("--out", required=True) ap.add_argument("--name", default="Aditya Arora") ap.add_argument("--handle", default="@thefaadguy") ap.add_argument("--avatar", default=str(REPO / "clients/aditya-arora/drafts/images/_logos/aditya-avatar.jpg")) ap.add_argument("--logo-dir", default=str(REPO / "clients/aditya-arora/drafts/images/_logos"), help="folder searched for {{slug}} brand logos") ap.add_argument("--font-size", type=int, default=47) args = ap.parse_args() body = html.escape(args.text.replace("\\n", "\n")) # emphasis markup (applied after escaping, so spans are safe to inject) body = re.sub(r"__([^_]+)__", r'\1', body) body = re.sub(r"~([^~]+)~", r'\1', body) # inline brand logos: {{slug}} -> resolved against --logo-dir logo_dir = Path(args.logo_dir) def logo(m): slug = m.group(1) for ext in (".svg", ".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".webp"): p = logo_dir / f"{slug}{ext}" if p.exists(): return f'' raise SystemExit(f"tweet-card: no logo named '{slug}' in {logo_dir}") has_logo = "{{" in body body = re.sub(r"\{\{([A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+)\}\}", logo, body) # logos are ~2em tall, so open up the leading only when they are present # file:// needs an absolute path, a relative one silently renders a blank circle avatar_abs = str(pathlib.Path(args.avatar).expanduser().resolve()) doc = TEMPLATE.format(font=FONT_STACK, avatar=avatar_abs, name=html.escape(args.name), handle=html.escape(args.handle), body=body, fsize=args.font_size, lh="1.52" if has_logo else "1.36") tmp = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "tweetcard.html" tmp.write_text(doc, encoding="utf-8") subprocess.run(["python3", str(REPO / "tools/html-to-png.py"), "--html", str(tmp), "--out", args.out, "--width", "1080", "--height", "1080"], check=True) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

content.text:
Scheduled, sir — **tomorrow, Wed 19 August, 10:00 AM IST** (job 986, draft 121, one pending job).

**Preview:** https://app.thesnowball.agency/preview-linkedin/2026-08-19-aditya-avtext-titan-ultratech

**The story:** Titan ₹4.50 lakh Cr vs UltraTech Cement ₹3.43 lakh Cr. UltraTech makes **205 million tonnes of cement a year — the most of any company outside China** — runs 30+ integrated plants and employs 86,000 people. Titan sells watches and jewellery, 90%+ of its income from gold, and the market pays it over ₹1 lakh Cr more. Verdict: **"India buys gold before bricks."** Card carries both real logos inline.

On the 200K target: I can't promise a number — reach is LinkedIn's call. But this is built on the precise formula that just produced 263,703 with Eternal vs Indian Oil, and every variable is deliberately set:

**Prestige inversion** — cement is the thing that literally builds the country; jewellery is a discretionary purchase, and it wins. **Universal daily-touch on both sides** — every Indian family has bought Tanishq for a wedding and lives in a house made of cement. That's the trait separating the 250K tier from the 20K tier. **Fresh foil category** — I deliberately avoided a second consecutive oil comparison after yesterday's; that repeat pattern is exactly what sank Eternal/Wipro to 16K. And Titan is our best-ever protagonist (269K on 23 July, 26 days ago, against a completely different opponent). There's a bonus layer too: Tata's crown jewel versus the Aditya Birla group's.

One judgement call in the fact-check: I dropped the revenue comparison. UltraTech's net sales (₹87,384 Cr) beat Titan's sales (₹76,797 Cr), but Titan's *total income* (₹88,136 Cr) edges ahead — the comparison flips depending on which line you pick, so commenters could argue it either way. Physical scale (tonnes, plants, employees) is unambiguous, so the post uses that instead.

Worth noting on yesterday's off-slot post: Bajaj Finance vs Infosys is at 14,867 after five hours, tracking well below the pattern. The 1 AM publish and same-day proximity to the Eternal post look like the cause rather than the topic — the IT-prestige angle itself has been our strongest. I'd hold to the single 10:00 AM slot going forward.
